body.statement: Can \(H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) produce one pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private estimator, without knowing \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\Theta_{\mathrm{sm}}\), whose risk is within the smallest possible logarithmic factor of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) simultaneously across sparse and dense occupancy, and can a matching adaptive lower bound determine that factor?
body.justification: Unknown smoothness is the first deployment-level uncertainty after the fixed-class frontier is settled, and privacy may make its penalty regime dependent.
body.gap: Cai et al. characterize adaptation for federated density estimation, while Kennedy et al. leave nonprivate CATE adaptation open; no result combines nuisance elbows, occupancy, and pure central privacy.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether one private release can be tuned for individualized-effect analysis without disclosing or prespecifying smoothness.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine the smallest simultaneous adaptation factor over the compact smoothness range \(\Theta_{\mathrm{sm}}\) for one pure-private scalar release.
obligation.obstruction: The base rho-star score family remains unconstructed, and the adaptive handle does not define the joint score array or its global replacement sensitivity. Without that geometry, neither a correlated-noise upper bound nor an adaptive testing lower bound has a well-typed object to analyze.
obligation.attempted: A finite multiscale release under basic composition was compared with the desired one-shot release. It yields the explicit benchmark below after replacing epsilon by epsilon divided by the number of scales, but it cannot identify whether this factor is necessary or can be reduced by correlation and post-processing.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved fixed-class ingredients show that any successful adaptive release
must control, on the same privacy transcript, both a dense scale satisfying
\(n\epsilon r^{1+d/\gamma}\asymp1\) and a sparse scale satisfying
\(n^2\epsilon r^{1+d/\gamma+d/q}\asymp1\).  Releasing \(J\) candidate
arrays separately by basic composition replaces \(\epsilon\) by
\(\epsilon/J\), which gives the explicit but generally nonoptimal benchmark
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee
 (n\epsilon/J)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)}\vee
 (n^2\epsilon/J)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.
\]
No conclusion about the smallest possible logarithmic factor follows until
the joint sensitivity or correlated-noise geometry of the one-shot array is
specified.
